THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
 ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:50064  CRL.RP No. 455 of 2017 CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE V SRISHANANDA  ORAL ORDER Heard Sri Gangadhar D.C, advocate representing Sri Harish Kumar, learned counsel for the revision petitioner and Sri K.S.Shreekantha, learned counsel for the respondent.
2. Parties present.
3. Having heard the parties, it is noticed that revision petitioner has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 324, 498A, 504 and 506 of the IPC and sentenced as under:
"The accused No.1 is sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 3 months and pay fine of Rs.2,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 324 of Indian Penal Code.
Further, the accused No.1 shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 6 months and pay fine of Rs.5,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code.
The accused No.1 shall pay fine of Rs.3,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 504 of Indian Penal Code.

Further the accused No.1 shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 3 months and pay fine of Rs.2,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 506 of Indian Penal Code.
NC: 2024:KHC:50064 Acting under Section 357(2) of Cr.P.C. out of fine amount of Rs.1,2000/-, Rs.10,000/- has to be paid to the complainant as compensation.
Supply free copy of the judgment to the accused No.1.
Issue conviction warrant."
4. Given the attendant facts and circumstances, having regard to the scope of the revisional jurisdiction as is held in the case of Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and another reported in T Ramesh vs Smt Nethravathi on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13839892/
2 (2012)9 SCC 460, order of conviction cannot be interfered by this Court, that too, in revisional jurisdiction.
5.

sentences.text: However, taking note of the fact that the revision petitioner and the de-facto complainant who pursued the matter by filing private complaint having remarried, sending the petitioner to prison at this distance of time would serve no purpose.

6. Instead, if the fine amount is enhanced to a sum of Rs.50,000/- and entire sum of Rs.50,000/- is ordered to be paid as compensation under Section 357 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to the defacto complainant, ends of justice would be met.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER (i) Criminal Revision Petition is allowed in part.

(ii) While maintaining the conviction of the accused for the offences punishable under Sections 324, 498A, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, the imprisonment ordered by the learned Trial Magistrate confirmed by the learned Judge in the First Appellate Court is set-aside, subject to payment of enhanced fine amount of Rs.50,000/- by the revision petitioner to the defacto complainant/P.W.1, under due identification, on or before 10.01.2025.

(iii) Failure to make the payment of enhanced fine amount would result in restoration of the order passed by learned Trial Magistrate confirmed by the learned Judge in the First Appellate Court, automatically.
